nodes.label: Heavy statements

nodes.label: Index efficiency

binding_groups.label: Index activity

nodes.label: Many light statements

nodes.label: System CPU

binding_groups.label: Page faults
binding_groups.unassessed_reason: Page-fault counts alone do not establish memory pressure. Minor faults need no disk read; major faults require correlation with memory availability and I/O latency.

nodes.label: LWLock contention

nodes.label: Network traffic

nodes.label: Paging and THP

nodes.label: I/O wait
nodes.summary: CPU idle time with outstanding I/O. Follow reads, writes and swap evidence; high wait is not CPU execution.

nodes.label: Network
nodes.summary: Host traffic and interface health, client transport, replication paths, TCP configuration and network access. Symptoms are not proof of a network root cause.

nodes.label: Traffic
nodes.summary: Per-interface receive, transmit and packet rates. Host traffic includes non-PostgreSQL processes and virtual interfaces may overlap.

nodes.label: Receive throughput
nodes.summary: Inbound byte rates by interface; link utilization is assessed only when that interface has an explicit current link speed.

nodes.label: Transmit throughput
nodes.summary: Outbound byte rates by interface. Do not add RX and TX to estimate full-duplex link utilization.

nodes.label: Packet processing
nodes.summary: Packet rates by interface; high rates become a processing concern only with system CPU pressure. Not a bandwidth limit.

nodes.label: Interface health
nodes.summary: Observed RX/TX errors and drops, with NIC and address context. Rates describe the collection window, not interface lifetime.

nodes.label: RX / TX errors
nodes.summary: Error rates per interface. Link, driver and queue investigation is needed; these counters do not identify the PostgreSQL path.

nodes.label: RX / TX drops
nodes.summary: Dropped and missed packets exposed by /proc/net/dev. Drops are not necessarily hardware failures or TCP retransmissions.

nodes.label: NICs and addresses
nodes.summary: Interface names, addresses, current link speeds and driver inventory; inactive or virtual NICs are not faults by themselves.

nodes.label: Client connections
nodes.summary: Client transport waits, connection demand, reconnects and disconnections. Application behavior may cause these symptoms.

nodes.label: ClientWrite waits
nodes.summary: Backends waiting to send data to clients: check slow consumers, result size and the network; the wait does not isolate the cause.

nodes.label: ClientRead waits
nodes.summary: Backends waiting for clients to send data. Idle clients and application think time are not network faults.

nodes.label: Connection capacity
nodes.summary: Connection and role limits, including local sockets; capacity pressure does not by itself prove a network fault.

nodes.label: Reconnect rate
nodes.summary: New sessions per second during the snapshot window; pooling and application connection reuse are possible contributors.

nodes.label: Frequent statements
nodes.summary: Statement call counts and query rates are context for chatty clients, not direct RTT measurements.

nodes.label: Connection failures
nodes.summary: Transport-specific SQLSTATEs and anchored server messages; abandoned clients may also reflect application exits. Query timeouts and administrator kills are not network evidence.

nodes.label: Replication transport
nodes.summary: WAL sending and receiving, streaming sessions and synchronous acknowledgement. Replay and disk delays are not automatically network problems.

nodes.label: WAL send backlog
nodes.summary: WAL generated but not sent and sent-to-write acknowledgement backlog; investigate sender CPU, transport and receiver writes separately.

binding_groups.label: Sender CPU and network traffic
binding_groups.unassessed_reason: Sender CPU and transmit rates describe activity; without CPU capacity or link capacity they cannot establish saturation.

nodes.label: WAL receiver
nodes.summary: Receiver streaming state and announced-to-received WAL gap; message age alone is not a transport fault.

nodes.label: Synchronous replies
nodes.summary: Missing synchronous quorum or commits waiting in SyncRep. Remote disk writes and replay may be responsible as well as transport.

nodes.label: Streaming topology
nodes.summary: Physical senders, logical subscriptions, slots and capacity as context. Apply errors and retained WAL are evaluated under database health.

nodes.label: Streaming disconnects
nodes.summary: Only transport disconnect events affect this node; archive failures, recovery conflicts and missing WAL are not proof of network failure.

nodes.label: TCP / UDP configuration
nodes.summary: Transport configuration is evidence for follow-up, not a measurement of RTT, TCP retransmissions or socket queues.

nodes.label: TCP and keepalives
nodes.summary: Kernel TCP buffers, congestion control, retries, keepalives and PostgreSQL connection timeouts. No universal configuration score.

nodes.label: UDP buffers
nodes.summary: Kernel UDP configuration; PostgreSQL client connections use TCP or Unix sockets, not UDP.

nodes.label: Access and encryption
nodes.summary: Network exposure, authentication rules, encrypted sessions and local socket access; these are security risks, not throughput measurements.

nodes.label: Listeners and firewall
nodes.summary: Listening addresses, host firewall and broad HBA networks.

nodes.label: TLS and GSS encryption
nodes.summary: Server TLS configuration, HBA enforcement, weak ciphers, remote unencrypted sessions and key permissions.

nodes.label: Authentication and HBA
nodes.summary: Authentication failures and permissive access rules; not evidence of transport saturation.

nodes.label: Unix socket access
nodes.summary: Local socket permissions are separate from TCP interfaces and host traffic.

nodes.label: Database health
nodes.summary: Breakages and imminent failures: errors, corruption, wraparound, locks, connections, replication.

nodes.label: Errors in the log
nodes.summary: ERROR, FATAL and PANIC records in the collected log window.

nodes.label: Crashes and corruption
nodes.summary: Crash recovery, checksum failures, corruption-hiding settings, collation drift.

nodes.label: Invalid objects
nodes.summary: Invalid indexes, unvalidated constraints, disabled triggers, tables without a key.

nodes.label: Wraparound and sequences
nodes.summary: Transaction id age against freeze limits; sequence exhaustion.

nodes.label: Autovacuum lag and bloat
nodes.summary: Tables overdue for vacuum, dead tuple share, bloat estimates.

nodes.label: Xmin horizon
nodes.summary: Long transactions, prepared transactions, slots and standby feedback that block cleanup.

nodes.label: Locks and deadlocks
nodes.summary: Blocked sessions, blocker chains, lock waits and deadlocks in the log.

binding_groups.label: Lock waits and terminations in logs

nodes.label: Connection exhaustion
nodes.summary: Connection usage against limits, refused connections in the log, sessions ended fatally or abandoned.

nodes.label: Replication
nodes.summary: Sender and replay lag, inactive slots, standby conflicts, synchronous replication.

nodes.label: WAL archiving
nodes.summary: Failed archive_command runs and WAL waiting to be archived.

nodes.label: Configuration and version
nodes.summary: Configuration file errors, pending restarts, end-of-life version, durability settings.

binding_groups.label: Settings and statistics resets
binding_groups.unassessed_reason: Settings and reset timestamps provide context for other rules. A settings inventory alone is not a configuration validation.

nodes.label: Observability gaps
nodes.summary: Missing pg_stat_statements, pg_stat_kcache, pg_wait_sampling, function tracking.

nodes.label: Running maintenance
nodes.summary: VACUUM, CREATE INDEX, CLUSTER and COPY operations in progress.

nodes.label: Platform inventory
nodes.summary: Kernel, distribution, hardware and process inventory.

binding_groups.label: Operating system and hardware platform
binding_groups.unassessed_reason: These measurements describe operating system and hardware platform. Activity volume alone has no universal healthy limit; capacity, latency or workload expectations are required for a health assessment.

binding_groups.label: Peripheral devices and power
binding_groups.unassessed_reason: These measurements describe peripheral devices and power. Activity volume alone has no universal healthy limit; capacity, latency or workload expectations are required for a health assessment.

binding_groups.unassessed_reason: These measurements describe network devices and addresses. Activity volume alone has no universal healthy limit; capacity, latency or workload expectations are required for a health assessment.

binding_groups.label: PostgreSQL processes and databases
binding_groups.unassessed_reason: These measurements describe postgresql processes and databases. Activity volume alone has no universal healthy limit; capacity, latency or workload expectations are required for a health assessment.

nodes.label: Database security
nodes.summary: Risk exposure: authentication, network, privileges, host hardening, audit.

nodes.label: Authentication
nodes.summary: Insecure pg_hba methods, remote superuser login, weak password hashing.

nodes.label: Network exposure
nodes.summary: Listen addresses, TLS enforcement and ciphers, firewall, unencrypted sessions.

nodes.label: Roles and cluster privileges
nodes.summary: Superuser and administrative login roles, membership reach, connection limits.

nodes.label: Object privileges and ownership
nodes.summary: PUBLIC and grantable privileges, SECURITY DEFINER functions, RLS gaps, owner drift.

nodes.label: Host hardening
nodes.summary: File and directory permissions, sudoers, secrets in environments, core dumps, encryption.

nodes.label: Audit and logging
nodes.summary: Security logging posture, pgAudit, risky and missing extensions.
